property_summary: After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was 0, c.initialized must be true (so the contract becomes initialized).
After seeding market from a fresh contract, getFreeKilo must succeed (not revert) for a new address and set its Kilos to STARTING_KILOS and lastCollect nonzero.

After a successful seedMarket call on an uninitialized market, the contract becomes initialized (initialized==true) and thus allows getFreeKilo to be called without reverting for a new address, resulting in Kilos for that address equal to STARTING_KILOS.

After seeding the market (when marketDrugs was previously zero) the contract must accept a subsequent getFreeKilo() call from a fresh caller without reverting (i.e., getFreeKilo succeeds and sets that caller's Kilos to STARTING_KILOS).

After seeding the market when marketDrugs was zero, the contract will have initialized==true allowing calculateDrugBuySimple to reflect the contract balance in its calculation (i.e., calculateDrugBuySimple(amount) equals calculateDrugBuy(amount, address(c).balance)).
After seeding a fresh market (marketDrugs == 0) the contract must become initialized so getFreeKilo can be called successfully by a new address, yielding that address's Kilos equals STARTING_KILOS.

For any caller, calling DrugDealer() sets c.initialized() to the same boolean value on the reference (true/false) as the contract's previous initialized only when CEO sets address? — more directly: In the reference implementation, calling seedMarket via any actor who seeds market (after DrugDealer is used to set ceo) results in initialized being set to true by seedMarket; the mutant removing initialized assignment can leave initialized false after seedMarket, so there exists an input (a fuzzed seeder amount and caller) where initialized differs; therefore the general rule: after seeding the market via seedMarket by the CEO, c.initialized() must be true — the mutant can produce a case where it is false.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0, initialized must be true and contract balance unchanged.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0, initialized becomes true (so the contract reports initialized == true via its public getter).
Calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0 makes initialized true afterwards and marketDrugs equal to the provided drugs.
Calling seedMarket when marketDrugs == 0 sets marketDrugs to the provided value and leaves the contract balance unchanged by the call.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was initially zero, marketDrugs equals the provided drugs and the contract's ether balance does not change due to the call.

After any call to DrugDealer() by the CEO address, the reference contract always leaves initialized==true, whereas the mutant that flips initialized in seedMarket can cause initialized to differ (false) after the same sequence for some fuzzed initial initialized value via seedMarket interactions.

For any caller and any initial marketDrugs, if seedMarket is called when marketDrugs==0 then initialized becomes true (reference always sets initialized true); the mutant that flips initialized can leave it false for some prior initialized value, so calling seedMarket should guarantee initialized==true.

For any initial boolean state and any caller, calling seedMarket when marketDrugs==0 sets initialized to true in the reference contract; the mutant that flips initialized can leave it false for some initial state, so the property is that after seedMarket initialized == true.

For any caller and any initial boolean initialized, calling seedMarket when marketDrugs==0 will result in c.initialized() == true in the reference (it sets initialized = true), but the mutant that flips initialized (initialized = !initialized) can leave it false for some initial value, so assert that initialized is true after seedMarket succeeds.

After a successful seedMarket(drugs) call when marketDrugs==0, the reference contract always ensures initialized becomes true (regardless of prior value), whereas the mutant that flips initialized (initialized = !initialized) will leave initialized false when it was false before the call, so there exist inputs (an initial initialized==false and calling seedMarket) that make the mutant differ.
After calling seedMarket with any drugs value, c.initialized() is true whenever marketDrugs() > 0.
After calling seedMarket(drugs) on a fresh market (marketDrugs == 0), c.initialized() becomes true whenever the provided drugs value is nonzero.

If seedMarket is called when marketDrugs==0, then afterwards either marketDrugs>0 or initialized==true (i.e., a zero-market seed cannot leave the contract both uninitialized and with zero market supply).
